questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A metre rule is used to measure the length of a wire and gives a reading of 24.65 cm. If the zero error of the rule is +0.05 cm, what is the corrected length?
questions.explanation: For a positive zero error, the correction is subtracted: 24.65 - 0.05 = 24.60 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The reading on a Vernier caliper has a main scale value of 3.2 cm and a Vernier scale coincidence at the 4th division (least count 0.01 cm). What is the total reading?
questions.explanation: Total reading = main scale + (Vernier division x least count) = 3.2 + (4 x 0.01) = 3.24 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A micrometer screw gauge has a pitch of 0.5 mm and 50 divisions on its thimble. What is its least count?
questions.explanation: Least count = pitch / number of divisions = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The density of a metal block of mass 540 g and volume 60 cm3 is
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 540/60 = 9 g/cm3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Express 0.0007821 to 3 significant figures.
questions.explanation: Counting from the first non-zero digit, the first three significant figures are 7, 8, 2, rounding gives 0.000782.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Which of the following is a base S.I. quantity?
questions.explanation: Luminous intensity (candela) is one of the seven S.I. base quantities; force, pressure, and energy are all derived quantities.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The dimension of pressure (force/area) is
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = (MLT-2)/L2 = ML-1T-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A student records five readings of the period of a pendulum as 2.0 s, 2.1 s, 1.9 s, 2.0 s, and 2.0 s. What is the mean period?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Which combination of fundamental quantities gives the S.I. unit of energy?
questions.explanation: Energy (joule) = force x distance = (kg m s-2)(m) = kg m2 s-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two lengths, 12.4 cm and 3.65 cm, are measured with instruments of different precision. Expressed to the correct number of significant figures, their sum is
questions.explanation: The least precise value (12.4 cm, 1 decimal place) limits the result, so the sum 16.05 cm is rounded to 16.1 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A boy walks 8 m east and then 6 m north. What is the magnitude of his resultant displacement?
questions.explanation: Resultant = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(64+36) = sqrt(100) = 10 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two forces of 6 N and 8 N act at right angles at a point. The angle the resultant makes with the 8 N force is
questions.explanation: tan(theta) = opposite/adjacent = 6/8 = 0.75, so theta = arctan(0.75) = 36.9 degrees from the 8 N force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A force of 20 N acts at 60 degrees to the horizontal. Its vertical component is approximately
questions.explanation: Vertical component = 20 sin 60 = 20 x 0.866 = 17.3 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed has magnitude only; velocity (its vector counterpart) has direction. Momentum, weight, and acceleration are all vectors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two equal forces of 10 N each act on a body such that the angle between them is 120 degrees. The magnitude of their resultant is
questions.explanation: R = sqrt(P^2+Q^2+2PQcos(theta)) = sqrt(100+100+200cos120) = sqrt(200-100) = sqrt(100) = 10 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A river flows at 3 m/s and a boat is steered directly across at 4 m/s relative to the water. The resultant speed of the boat relative to the bank is
questions.explanation: Since the velocities are perpendicular, resultant = sqrt(3^2+4^2) = sqrt(25) = 5 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Three coplanar forces of 5 N, 5 N, and 5 N act on a particle such that it remains in equilibrium. The angle between any two adjacent forces must be
questions.explanation: Three equal forces keep a particle in equilibrium only when arranged symmetrically at 120 degrees to each other, forming a closed equilateral triangle of forces.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A vector of magnitude 10 units is resolved into two perpendicular components. If one component is 6 units, the other component is
questions.explanation: Using Pythagoras: other component = sqrt(10^2-6^2) = sqrt(100-36) = sqrt(64) = 8 units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A car accelerates uniformly from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 4 seconds. Its acceleration is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A stone is dropped from a height of 45 m. How long does it take to reach the ground? (g = 10 m/s2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upward with a velocity of 30 m/s. What maximum height does it reach? (g = 10 m/s2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A car moving at 20 m/s decelerates uniformly at 4 m/s2. How long does it take to stop?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An object thrown horizontally from a cliff 20 m high with a speed of 15 m/s lands how far from the base of the cliff? (g = 10 m/s2)
questions.explanation: Time to fall: t = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(40/10) = 2 s. Horizontal range = speed x t = 15 x 2 = 30 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A body of mass 5 kg initially moving at 4 m/s is acted on by a force for 3 s, increasing its velocity to 10 m/s. The magnitude of the force is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A bullet of mass 0.02 kg moving at 300 m/s embeds in a stationary block of mass 1.98 kg. What is the velocity of the block and bullet immediately after impact?
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum: (0.02)(300) = (2.0)v, so v = 6/2.0 = 3 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A body moves in a circle of radius 2 m at a constant speed of 4 m/s. Its centripetal acceleration is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A car of mass 1000 kg moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest by a constant braking force in 5 s. The braking force is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two objects of masses 3 kg and 2 kg moving towards each other at 4 m/s and 6 m/s respectively collide and stick together. Taking the 3 kg direction as positive, the velocity after collision is
questions.explanation: Momentum: (3x4) + (2x-6) = 12-12 = 0. Combined mass = 5 kg, so v = 0/5 = 0 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An object undergoes SHM with amplitude 0.2 m and angular frequency 5 rad/s. Its maximum velocity is
questions.explanation: Maximum velocity in SHM = omega x amplitude = 5 x 0.2 = 1.0 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A projectile is fired at 40 m/s at 30 degrees to the horizontal. Its time of flight is approximately (g = 10 m/s2)
questions.explanation: Vertical component = 40 sin30 = 20 m/s. Time of flight = 2u_y/g = 40/10 = 4 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The gravitational force between two masses of 4 kg and 9 kg separated by 3 m is (G = 6.67 x 10^-11 Nm2/kg2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A man weighs 700 N on Earth's surface. What would his mass be? (g = 10 m/s2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: At what height above the Earth's surface (radius R) does the value of g reduce to a quarter of its surface value?
questions.explanation: g at height h is g_s(R/(R+h))^2. For g to be a quarter, (R/(R+h))^2 = 1/4, so R+h = 2R, giving h = R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An astronaut's mass is 80 kg on Earth. On the Moon, where gravitational field strength is about 1/6 that of Earth, his weight is approximately (g_Earth = 10 m/s2)
questions.explanation: Weight on Moon = mass x g_moon = 80 x (10/6) = 133.3 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A satellite orbits the Earth at a radius where its orbital period is 90 minutes. As the orbital radius increases, the orbital period
questions.explanation: By Kepler's third law, T^2 is proportional to r^3, so a larger orbital radius means a longer orbital period.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The escape velocity from a planet of mass M and radius R is given by
questions.explanation: Escape velocity is derived by equating kinetic energy to gravitational potential energy: 0.5mv^2 = GMm/R, giving v = sqrt(2GM/R).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A uniform beam of length 4 m and weight 60 N is balanced on a pivot at its centre. A load of 40 N is placed 1 m from the pivot on one side. Where must a 20 N load be placed on the other side to balance the beam?
questions.explanation: Taking moments: 40 x 1 = 20 x d, so d = 40/20 = 2 m from the pivot.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A uniform ladder of weight 200 N and length 5 m rests on a smooth wall and rough floor. If the ladder makes an angle of 60 degrees with the floor, which factor most affects whether it stays in equilibrium?
options: The material of the wall alone
The frictional force at the floor
questions.explanation: Since the wall is smooth (frictionless), only friction at the floor provides the horizontal force needed to prevent the ladder from slipping.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A see-saw of length 6 m is pivoted at its centre. A child of weight 300 N sits 2 m from the pivot. Where should a 200 N child sit on the other side for balance?
questions.explanation: Clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment: 300 x 2 = 200 x d, so d = 600/200 = 3 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Three forces of 10 N, 10 N, and 10 N act on a ring in equilibrium, forming a closed triangle when drawn to scale. This illustrates
options: the law of conservation of momentum
questions.explanation: When three concurrent forces are in equilibrium, they can be represented in magnitude and direction by the three sides of a closed triangle, taken in order.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A body of weight 100 N hangs from two strings inclined at 30 degrees and 60 degrees to the vertical support beam, meeting at a point. Which principle is used to find the tensions in the strings?
options: Lami's theorem or resolution of forces
questions.explanation: For three concurrent coplanar forces in equilibrium, Lami's theorem (or resolving forces into components) is used to determine unknown tensions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A metre rule is balanced at the 40 cm mark when a mass of 60 g is hung at the 10 cm mark. What is the mass of the metre rule, assumed to act at the 50 cm mark?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the 40 cm pivot: 60 g is 30 cm from the pivot, and the rule's weight (at 50 cm) is 10 cm from the pivot. So m x 10 = 60 x 30, giving m = 1800/10 = 180 g.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A force of 15 N moves an object through a distance of 8 m in the direction of the force. The work done is
questions.explanation: Work = force x distance = 15 x 8 = 120 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A body of mass 2 kg moving at 6 m/s has kinetic energy of

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An object of mass 5 kg is raised to a height of 4 m. Its gain in potential energy is (g = 10 m/s2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A machine does 3000 J of work in 15 seconds. Its power output is
questions.explanation: Power = work/time = 3000/15 = 200 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ball of mass 0.5 kg falls freely from a height of 20 m. Its speed just before hitting the ground is (g = 10 m/s2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A pump raises 200 kg of water through a height of 15 m every 10 seconds. Taking g = 10 m/s2, the power of the pump is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A spring with force constant 200 N/m is compressed by 0.1 m. The elastic potential energy stored is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An engine of power 5000 W is used to lift a load at a constant velocity of 2 m/s. The maximum load it can lift is (g = 10 m/s2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: By the principle of conservation of energy, a pendulum bob released from a height of 0.45 m will have a speed at its lowest point of approximately (g = 10 m/s2)
questions.explanation: mgh = 0.5mv^2, so v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2x10x0.45) = sqrt(9) = 3 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A crane lifts a 500 kg load through 10 m in 25 s. What is the power developed? (g = 10 m/s2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A block of mass 10 kg rests on a horizontal surface with a coefficient of static friction of 0.4. The maximum frictional force before it starts to slide is (g = 10 m/s2)
questions.explanation: Maximum friction = mu x Normal force = 0.4 x (10x10) = 0.4 x 100 = 40 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A lever has a load of 300 N placed 0.5 m from the pivot and an effort applied 1.5 m from the pivot. The mechanical advantage of the lever is
questions.explanation: For a lever, M.A. = load arm ratio inversely, but here M.A. = effort distance/load distance = 1.5/0.5 = 3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An inclined plane of length 10 m raises a load to a height of 2 m. Its velocity ratio is
questions.explanation: Velocity ratio for an inclined plane = length/height = 10/2 = 5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A pulley system has a velocity ratio of 4. If an effort of 150 N raises a load of 500 N, the efficiency of the system is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A block weighing 50 N is pulled at constant velocity along a rough horizontal surface by a horizontal force of 15 N. The coefficient of kinetic friction is
questions.explanation: At constant velocity, applied force = friction force = 15 N. mu = friction/normal = 15/50 = 0.3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A screw jack has a pitch of 5 mm and a handle of length 35 cm. Its velocity ratio is approximately
questions.explanation: V.R. = (2 x pi x handle length)/pitch = (2 x 3.142 x 350)/5 = 2199.1/5 = 439.8, approximately 440.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a wheel and axle system, the wheel has a radius of 20 cm and the axle has a radius of 4 cm. The velocity ratio is
questions.explanation: V.R. = radius of wheel/radius of axle = 20/4 = 5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A block of mass 8 kg is on the verge of sliding down a rough incline set at 30 degrees to the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the incline is approximately
questions.explanation: At the point of sliding, mu = tan(theta) = tan30 = 0.577.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A wire of original length 2 m and cross-sectional area 1 x 10^-6 m2 extends by 1 mm under a load of 100 N. Its Young's modulus is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A spring extends by 4 cm when a load of 8 N is applied, obeying Hooke's law. What load would produce an extension of 10 cm?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A liquid of density 800 kg/m3 exerts a pressure at a depth of 5 m of (g = 10 m/s2)
questions.explanation: Pressure = density x g x h = 800 x 10 x 5 = 40000 Pa.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A solid object of volume 2 x 10^-4 m3 is fully submerged in water (density 1000 kg/m3). The upthrust on it is (g = 10 m/s2)
questions.explanation: Upthrust = weight of displaced fluid = density x volume x g = 1000 x 2x10^-4 x 10 = 2 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A hydraulic press has a small piston of area 5 cm2 and a large piston of area 100 cm2. An effort of 50 N on the small piston produces a load force of
questions.explanation: Pressure is transmitted equally: F2 = F1 x (A2/A1) = 50 x (100/5) = 1000 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A capillary tube of radius 0.5 mm is dipped in water. The rise of water due to surface tension is best explained by
options: adhesive forces between water and glass exceeding cohesive forces within water
questions.explanation: Capillary rise occurs because adhesion between the liquid and the tube wall exceeds cohesion within the liquid, pulling the liquid surface upward along the walls.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An object weighs 50 N in air and 30 N when fully submerged in water. Its upthrust in water is
questions.explanation: Upthrust = apparent loss in weight = weight in air - weight in water = 50 - 30 = 20 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A gas occupies 400 cm3 at a pressure of 100 kPa. At constant temperature, if the pressure increases to 200 kPa, the new volume is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An elastic material is stretched beyond its elastic limit. Which statement is true?
options: It behaves identically to before loading
It will not return to its original length after the load is removed
Its extension remains proportional to the applied force
questions.explanation: Beyond the elastic limit, permanent (plastic) deformation occurs, so the material does not fully recover its original dimensions when unloaded.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A mass of 2 kg of water is heated from 20 degC to 80 degC. If the specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J/kgK, the heat energy required is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A gas at 27 degC is heated at constant pressure until its volume doubles. What is the new temperature in degrees Celsius?
questions.explanation: By Charles' Law, V1/T1 = V2/T2 in Kelvin: 300 K doubles to 600 K, which is 600-273 = 327 degC.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The quantity of heat needed to melt 0.5 kg of ice at 0 degC (specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 336000 J/kg) is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A block of copper of mass 200 g absorbs 1800 J of heat, raising its temperature by 25 degC. The specific heat capacity of copper is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A steel rod of length 2 m and linear expansivity 1.2 x 10^-5 /K is heated through 50 K. Its increase in length is
questions.explanation: Extension = L x alpha x deltaT = 2 x 1.2x10^-5 x 50 = 1.2x10^-3 m = 1.2 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: On the Kelvin scale, absolute zero corresponds to
questions.explanation: Absolute zero, the theoretical lowest possible temperature, is -273.15 degC (approximately -273 degC), equal to 0 K.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A fixed mass of gas at constant volume has an initial pressure of 100 kPa at 300 K. When heated to 450 K, its new pressure is
questions.explanation: By Pressure Law (constant volume), P1/T1 = P2/T2: P2 = 100 x (450/300) = 150 kPa.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Heat transfer through a metal rod without bulk movement of the metal itself is called
questions.explanation: Conduction transfers heat energy via molecular/electron vibration and collision through a material, without the material itself flowing, unlike convection.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A calorimeter of negligible heat capacity contains 0.3 kg of water at 20 degC. A 0.1 kg piece of metal at 100 degC is dropped in, and the final temperature is 25 degC. Taking specific heat capacity of water as 4200 J/kgK, the specific heat capacity of the metal is approximately
questions.explanation: Heat gained by water = 0.3x4200x5 = 6300 J = heat lost by metal = 0.1 x c x 75. So c = 6300/7.5 = 840 J/kgK.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and wavelength 4 m. Its speed is
questions.explanation: Speed = frequency x wavelength = 50 x 4 = 200 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A sound wave travels 340 m in 1 second in air. If its wavelength is 0.68 m, its frequency is
questions.explanation: f = v/wavelength = 340/0.68 = 500 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An observer hears an echo from a cliff 3 seconds after producing a sound. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, the distance to the cliff is
questions.explanation: Distance = (speed x time)/2 = (340 x 3)/2 = 1020/2 = 510 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A stationary wave is formed on a string fixed at both ends, length 1.2 m, vibrating in its fundamental mode. The wavelength of the wave is
questions.explanation: For the fundamental mode on a string fixed at both ends, wavelength = 2L = 2 x 1.2 = 2.4 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A closed pipe of length 0.5 m resonates at its fundamental frequency. Taking the speed of sound as 340 m/s, this fundamental frequency is
questions.explanation: For a closed pipe, fundamental wavelength = 4L = 2.0 m. f = v/wavelength = 340/2.0 = 170 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two sound waves of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. The beat frequency heard is
questions.explanation: Beat frequency = difference between the two frequencies = 260 - 256 = 4 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The phenomenon in which the observed frequency of a sound changes due to relative motion between source and observer is called
questions.explanation: The Doppler effect describes the apparent change in frequency of a wave due to relative motion between the source and the observer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A wave of period 0.02 s has a frequency of

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Which property distinguishes transverse waves from longitudinal waves?
options: Particle vibration is perpendicular to the direction of wave travel
They require a medium to propagate
They cannot travel through a vacuum
questions.explanation: In transverse waves, particles oscillate perpendicular to the direction of energy propagation, unlike longitudinal waves where particles oscillate parallel to it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The critical angle for a medium with refractive index 1.5 is approximately

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A convex lens forms a real, inverted image twice the size of the object. If the object distance is 15 cm, the image distance is
questions.explanation: Magnification = v/u, so 2 = v/15, giving v = 30 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An object 5 cm tall is placed in front of a lens and forms an image 15 cm tall. The linear magnification produced is
questions.explanation: Magnification = image height/object height = 15/5 = 3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A ray of light passing through a triangular glass prism is bent towards the base of the prism. This bending is due to
options: refraction at the two prism surfaces
questions.explanation: As light enters and exits the prism's two inclined surfaces, it refracts at each surface, bending the overall ray path towards the base.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The image formed in a plane mirror is
options: virtual, laterally inverted, and the same size as the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror always produces a virtual, upright, laterally inverted image that is the same size as the object, located as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A converging lens of focal length 25 cm is used as a magnifying glass. Its power in dioptres is
questions.explanation: Power = 1/f(in metres) = 1/0.25 = 4 D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: White light splitting into its component colours when passing through a prism is called
questions.explanation: Dispersion occurs because different wavelengths (colours) of light refract by different amounts in the prism, spreading white light into a spectrum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A current of 2 A flows through a resistor of 15 ohms for 10 seconds. The quantity of charge that flows is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Three resistors of 2 ohms, 3 ohms, and 5 ohms are connected in series to a 20 V battery. The current flowing in the circuit is
questions.explanation: Total resistance = 2+3+5 = 10 ohms. I = V/R = 20/10 = 2 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two resistors of 4 ohms and 6 ohms are connected in parallel. Their combined resistance is
